cases.subject: accountancy
cases.body: Which investment can qualify as a cash equivalent under the stated maturity test?
options: A short-term deposit acquired today and maturing in two months, readily convertible with insignificant value risk
Equity shares held for resale with no stated redemption date
A five-year government bond acquired today
A deposit maturing four months after acquisition

sources.quote: “Cash equivalents” means short-term highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value. An investment normally qualifies as cash equivalents only when it has a short maturity, of say, three months or less from the date of acquisition.

cases.subject: accountancy
cases.body: A garment maker reports two cash receipts: payment from customers for delivered garments and proceeds from selling an old cutting machine. Which classification is correct?
options: Customer payment is operating; machine-sale proceeds are investing
Customer payment is investing; machine-sale proceeds are operating

sources.quote: Operating activities are the activities that constitute the primary or main activities of an enterprise. These are the principal revenue generating activities (or the main activities) of the enterprise and these activities are not investing or financing activities. Examples of cash flows from operating activities are cash receipts from sale of goods and the rendering of services.

cases.subject: accountancy
cases.body: What is the primary purpose of presenting operating, investing and financing cash flows separately?
options: To show only the profit earned in the period
To provide information about cash inflows and outflows under the three activity heads
To replace the income statement and balance sheet
To report only cash held at year end

sources.quote: The primary objective of cash flow statement is to provide useful information about cash flows (inflows and outflows) of an enterprise during a particular period under various heads, i.e., operating activities, investing activities and financing activities.

cases.subject: accountancy
cases.body: A company pays cash to acquire a delivery van for use over several years. Which activity is this cash outflow?
options: It is excluded because the van is a fixed asset

sources.quote: Examples of cash flows arising from investing activities are cash payments to acquire fixed assets including intangibles and cash receipt from disposal of fixed assets including intangibles.

cases.subject: business_studies
cases.body: A new firm has approved its structure and now identifies workforce needs before recruiting and selecting people. Which management function is it carrying out?

sources.quote: Staffing has been described as the managerial function of filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation structure. This is achieved by, first of all, identifying requirement of work force, followed by recruitment, selection, placement, promotion, appraisal and development of personnel.

cases.subject: business_studies
cases.body: An employee already doing the job receives instruction to update job skills and prepare for greater responsibility. Which staffing activity is described?

sources.quote: Employees need to be trained for upgradation of knowledge and skills and for preparing for higher responsibilities. Staff training and development is another important aspect of the staffing process.

cases.subject: business_studies
cases.body: A buyer seeks relief after a product falls short of the seller’s stated expectations. Which consumer right most directly addresses obtaining that relief?

sources.quote: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 provides for six rights of consumers. The right to seek redressal gives the consumer a right to get relief against unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practices or unscrupulous exploitation in case the product or service falls short of expectations.

cases.subject: business_studies
cases.body: A customer files a complaint and asks the company to consider it. Which consumer right is directly engaged by the opportunity to present the complaint?

sources.quote: The consumer has a right to file a complaint and to be heard in case of dissatisfaction with a good or a service.

cases.subject: economics
cases.body: A student’s total utility rises from 28 units after four units of a good to 30 after five. What is the marginal utility of the fifth unit?

sources.quote: Marginal utility (MU) is the change in total utility due to consumption of one additional unit of a commodity. Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility states that marginal utility from consuming each additional unit of a commodity declines as its consumption increases, while keeping consumption of other commodities constant.

cases.subject: economics
cases.body: A consumer ranks three bundles from most preferred to least preferred but does not assign them numerical utility values. Which approach is being used?

sources.quote: The consumer does not measure utility in numbers, though she often ranks various consumption bundles. This forms the starting point of ordinal utility analysis.

cases.subject: economics
cases.body: Two bundles lie on the same indifference curve. What does the source-supported interpretation say about the consumer’s evaluation of them?
options: The bundle farther right must be preferred
They contain identical quantities of both goods

sources.quote: All points on an indifference curve represent bundles which are considered indifferent by the consumer.

cases.subject: economics
cases.body: A room heater gives the same person different utility in Chennai in summer and Ladakh in winter. Which explanation is supported?
options: Utility can change with place and time
Utility is always identical for the same person
Utility depends only on the product’s price
The heater has become a different commodity

sources.quote: Utility that one individual gets from the commodity can change with change in place and time.

cases.subject: english
cases.body: In the workshop passage, what did Arun ask the apprentice to compare before deciding what to do?
options: The second-hand movement and the escapement sound
The clock’s colour and the tray depth
The room’s temperature and the tool length
The apprentice’s notes and the village timetable
cases.passage_text: When the village clock stopped, Arun carried it to the repair room and placed its screws in a shallow tray. His apprentice wanted to replace the whole mechanism immediately. Arun first asked her to compare the movement of the second hand with the sound of the escapement. They found a thread caught near one gear. After removing it, they watched the clock for an hour before declaring the repair complete. The apprentice later said the waiting had taught her as much as the repair.

cases.subject: english
cases.body: In the ferry passage, the word “fresh” in “fresh date” means:
cases.passage_text: At the river landing, Dev kept a small board listing the ferry times. The printed timetable had been washed away in the monsoon, so he copied the operator’s new schedule in chalk each morning. When the current grew too strong, the operator cancelled the noon crossing and Dev crossed that line through. A visitor complained that the board had changed. Dev pointed to the fresh date written at the top and said that an accurate change was more useful than a familiar but unsafe promise.
